shower.thought: We assume our memories are reliable because we have no way to fact-check the ones that matter most.
You've probably had the same conversation with different people and never realized you were the inconsistent one.
The only reason you believe you have a personality is because you haven't been in enough different situations to prove yourself wrong.
Every photo you take is evidence that you cared about this moment—which means the moments you don't photograph might matter more.
You're nostalgic for versions of yourself that probably didn't actually exist the way you remember them.
Most of what you know about your own childhood comes from stories other people told you.
The things you're most confident about are often the ones you've thought about the least.
You can't prove the last five minutes actually happened the way you think it did.
We spend our whole lives trying to figure out who we are, but we're constantly becoming someone different.
Your anxiety might just be your brain practicing for problems that will never happen.
The people who seem to have it all figured out are just better at pretending.
You've never actually seen your own face—only reflections and photos, which are all slightly wrong.
We call it "finding yourself" when really we're just deciding who we want to be this year.
Most of your decisions are made by a version of you that doesn't fully exist anymore by the time you're living with the consequences.
Comfort is just another name for the patterns you're too tired to question.
You know less about the people closest to you than you think, because you stopped asking questions once they became familiar.
The scariest thing isn't that we're running out of time—it's that we might not even notice.
You're probably better at something than you think you are, but you'll never try hard enough to find out.
Everything you regret is something you once thought was a good idea.
The people you miss most are often the ones you stopped trying for, not the ones who left.

darkjoke.thought:
I told my friend he was adopted.
He said, "I know." I said, "No, I mean today. Mom just called."

My therapist asked if I had any coping mechanisms.
I said, "Yeah, I'm talking to you about it."

I'm reading a book on the history of glue.
Can't put it down.

My dad said, "Son, I'm very disappointed in you."
I said, "Hi, Very Disappointed, I'm Dad."
He left when I was three, so the timing was perfect.

I tried to console my friend about his breakup.
I said, "There are plenty of fish in the sea."
He said, "She was allergic to seafood anyway."

My insurance company denied my claim.
I guess they really *don't* want me to get better.

I asked my boss for a raise.
He said, "You're doing great work, but the economy is tough right now."
Two weeks later he bought a new car.

People keep asking me if I'm okay.
I've started saying no just to see what happens.
So far, nobody's followed up.

My friend said he's been going to the gym every day.
I said, "That's great, how do you feel?"
He said, "Tired and poor."

I told my mom I was seeing a therapist.
She said, "That's wonderful, honey."
I said, "No, he's just standing there. I haven't paid him yet."

My ex texted me, "I miss you."
So I blocked her number.
Can't be too careful with technology these days.

I went to a self-help seminar last week.
The guy said, "You need to take control of your life."
So I left without paying.

My doctor said I need to cut back on caffeine.
I said, "When?"
He said, "After you're done vibrating."

I asked my accountant if I'm in financial trouble.
He said, "Define trouble."
I said, "Your face right now."

I told my kid that Santa isn't real.
He cried for an hour.
Then he asked about the Easter Bunny.
I said, "He's fine, just very depressed."

My friend asked why I never talk about my feelings.
I said, "Because every time I do, people get uncomfortable."
He said, "That's not—"
I said, "See?"

I got a fortune cookie that said, "A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step."
The next one said, "Please stop eating our cookies and go outside."

My therapist asked me to describe my childhood in one word.
I said, "Brief."
She said, "That's sad."
I said, "No, I'm an only child. It was actually pretty quiet."

I applied for life insurance.
They asked if I had any pre-existing conditions.
I said, "Yeah, existence."
They're still processing it.

My friend said he's never felt better about himself.
I asked what changed.
He said, "I stopped comparing myself to other people."
I said, "That must be nice."
He said, "Why, do you compare yourself to me?"
